brief: Privorotsky (GS) frames yesterday's selloff as de-grossing finally spilling from fundamental long/short into systematic strategies. Unconstrained momentum is now in its worst drawdown since the GFC outside COVID. Losses hit TMT, Asian long/short and multi-strat, popular longs down and popular shorts up, though Korea held up better than feared. AI underperformed SPX ex-AI by the most since the DeepSeek moment, with Bloom Energy and WDC falling despite strong prints. He argues the issue is not AI demand, which remains robust, but a repricing of the cost of capital funding the buildout, forcing capex cuts, delayed deployment or equity funding, none supportive of equity prices. That dynamic is also pulling down growth expectations and relieving duration, AI losing while bonds win, though the relief could reverse if AI stabilizes. Separately, simultaneous PHP, Java and Python vulnerabilities look bullish for cybersecurity spending, and crude's breakout reflects a Gulf geopolitical risk premium he calls binary: a contained strike could trigger a sell-the-news unwind, while a retaliatory hit to energy chokepoints would tighten balances further.
